title: 🌍 Global Trade Match
description: Test your knowledge of world trade! Match countries with their top exports, currencies, and major trade agreements. From Indian spices to Japanese electronics, discover how the global economy connects us all!
learning_objectives: Understand major global trade patterns and export economies
Learn about world currencies and exchange systems
Identify key international trade agreements and organizations

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: Tap a card to flip it and reveal either a country or a trade description
Tap a second card to try to match the country with its exports and currency
If the pair matches, both cards stay revealed and you earn 15 points
If they don't match, both cards flip back -- remember their positions!
Match all 8 country-trade pairs before the 2-minute timer runs out
tips: Think about each country's geography and natural resources to guide your guesses
Currency symbols on the back cards are helpful clues -- learn to recognise them
Avoid random flipping! Each miss costs 3 points, so recall card positions carefully
Faster completion earns a time bonus of 2 points per second remaining

pairs.back: Major iron ore & coal exporter, A$ (Dollar)

glossary_terms.definition: The total monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period. It is the most widely used measure of a nation's overall economic output and health.

A situation where a country imports more goods and services than it exports, meaning more money flows out of the country than comes in through trade. The opposite -- exporting more than importing -- is called a trade surplus.

A tax or duty imposed by a government on imported goods and services. Tariffs are used to protect domestic industries from foreign competition, generate government revenue, or as leverage in trade negotiations between countries.

An international organization established in 1995 that sets and enforces the rules of global trade between nations. With 164 member countries, the WTO resolves trade disputes, reduces trade barriers, and promotes free and fair international commerce.

An association of major emerging economies originally comprising Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa. BRICS nations represent over 40% of the world's population and a significant share of global GDP, and they collaborate on trade, development, and financial reform.

achievements.title: 🏆 Perfect Memory
achievements.description: Match all 8 pairs without a single wrong flip! Zero misses means you truly know your global trade.

achievements.title: ⚡ Speed Trader
achievements.description: Finish all matches in under 60 seconds! You trade knowledge faster than Wall Street trades stocks.
achievements.condition: Complete the game in under 60 seconds

achievements.title: 🌐 Global Scholar
achievements.description: Complete the game with a score of 100 or higher. Your world trade knowledge is truly impressive!
achievements.condition: Finish with a total score of 100 or more

win_conditions.description: Match all 8 country-trade pairs before the 120-second timer runs out! Fewer wrong flips = higher score. Can you match every country to its exports and currency on the first try?

coaching_moment: The skills you're building today compound over time. Accuracy matters more than speed — a small delay for correctness pays big dividends later.
cultural_context: India is among the world's most climate-vulnerable nations. Environmental thinking is increasingly integrated into India's school curricula under NEP 2020, preparing students for the sustainability challenges of India's development.
reflection_prompt: What pattern did you start to recognize as you played? How will you use it next time?
